Please Consider the Situation of Ukrainian Dota 2 Players
7 hours ago
[ФР] Дикограй
Sometimes we disconnect from matches through no fault of our own because of circumstances beyond our control.

Another problem is that even when Ukrainian players search for matches without selecting the Russian region, the chances of encountering Russian players remain very high. This makes it difficult to avoid toxic interactions and repeated reports from players who may target us because of our nationality.


We ask for a system that can distinguish intentional griefing from circumstances beyond a player's control and prevent the abuse of the reporting system.

Currently, 3 out of every 5 matches are extremely toxic—there are so many new accounts, which I’m certain belong to veteran players whose main accounts have very low behavior scores; they just create a new account and keep on being just as toxic. Behavior & Comms Score 3.0: Definitive Overhaul Blueprint
22 Oct @ 3:22am
Azure
Originally posted by sky3tone:
The most absurd thing about the Behavior Score system is that a first-time Dota player can get reported by their entire team for playing poorly—without having uttered a single word—and end up losing microphone.
You would be report even if you didn't swear—or even if you didn't say a word.

Additionally, multi-reports from a single party are throttled and consolidated into a single instance (Weight = 1), while report-spam accounts have their feedback weight calibrated to zero

A well-designed moderation infrastructure must differentiate between a lack of skill & intentional malicious behavior. We need automated pre-validation filters to neutralize toxic report-spam loops, rather than blind, volume-based punitive automation
